messages.content:
Implement strict decoding for a paginated release manifest.

Export:

```go
type Release struct {
    ID        int
    Name      string
    Published time.Time
}

type ReleasePage struct {
    Items      []Release
    NextCursor int
}

func DecodeReleasePage(data []byte) (ReleasePage, error)
```

The accepted JSON value must be an object containing exactly two required fields: `items` and `next_cursor`. `items` must be an array of objects containing exactly `id`, `name`, and `published`. IDs must be positive and unique within the page, names must be non-empty, and publication dates must use the exact `YYYY-MM-DD` form and represent real calendar dates. `next_cursor` must be non-negative. Unknown fields, missing fields, `null`, trailing JSON values, and malformed JSON are errors.

Object member names are compared case-sensitively after JSON string escape decoding. The root object must contain `items` and `next_cursor` exactly once each. Every item object must contain `id`, `name`, and `published` exactly once each. Repeated member names are errors, even if their values are equal; this includes different JSON spellings that decode to the same member name. Member order is unrestricted. JSON-escaped spellings of the required names are valid when their decoded spelling matches exactly and occurs only once.

Thus, `items` together with `\u0069tems` is a duplicate, a sole `\u0069tems` is valid, and `ITEMS` is unknown rather than an alternative spelling of `items`. Equal-valued duplicates, conflicting duplicates, and null-then-valid duplicates all fail. Duplicate checking is local to each object: `id` in two different item objects is not a duplicate member, although equal numeric ID values still violate the separate page-wide ID uniqueness rule.

JSON numbers for IDs and the cursor must decode directly into the native Go `int` type. Only integer tokens representable as `int` are valid: quoted numbers, booleans, fractions, exponent notation, and overflow are errors. IDs must be greater than zero and the cursor must be at least zero. Native negative-zero integer decoding remains valid for the cursor.

Names are valid when their decoded string is non-empty. Do not trim or normalize them; a whitespace-only non-empty name is valid and its exact decoded content must be preserved.

Dates must retain the exact `time.Parse("2006-01-02", value)` semantics followed by an exact format round trip. Calendar-invalid dates, non-padded forms, and timestamp suffixes are errors. Successful dates are returned at midnight UTC.

Preserve item order. An empty `items` array is valid and must produce a non-nil empty slice. Ordinary JSON whitespace before and after the single value is allowed. Do not modify `data`, and do not expose storage backed by it. Return exactly the zero value `ReleasePage{}` with every error; error wording and concrete error types are unspecified.

Return one complete standard-library-only source file in package `solution`. Do not include package `main` or a `main` function.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.

Implement an in-memory workshop registry. Export exactly `{ createWorkshopRegistry }` using CommonJS.

`createWorkshopRegistry(initialHosts = [])` accepts an array of host objects. Each host must be a non-null, non-array object with exactly the own fields `{ id, name }`. Required fields may be enumerable or non-enumerable, but inherited fields do not satisfy the schema. Extra own string fields, extra own symbol fields, and missing fields are invalid. Both values must be strings whose raw length is greater than zero; whitespace-only values are valid and all strings are preserved verbatim. Host IDs are unique and match exactly, including whitespace and case.

The function returns exactly `{ register, list }`.

`register(input)` requires a non-null, non-array object with exactly the own fields `{ name, kind, address, host }`, under the same own-field rules. `name` and `address` must be strings whose raw length is greater than zero, so whitespace-only strings are valid. `kind` must be exactly one of `lab`, `kitchen`, `garden`, or `studio`.

`host` must have exactly one of these shapes under the same own-field rules:
- `{ id }`, where `id` is a raw-length-nonzero string exactly matching an existing host ID.
- `{ newHost }`, where `newHost` has exactly the own fields `{ id, name }`, both raw-length-nonzero strings. The new ID must not already exist.

No other host-selection shape is valid. Do not impose any additional prototype or plain-object restriction.

Workshop names are unique after applying `name.trim().toLowerCase()`. Consequently, whitespace-only workshop names are valid but all normalize to the empty string and collide with one another. On a duplicate workshop name or host ID, throw `RangeError`. For malformed data or an unknown selected host, throw `TypeError`.

Successful registration returns a detached snapshot `{ name, kind, address, host: { id, name } }` containing the resolved host. `list()` returns detached snapshots of all workshops in registration order. Preserve stored strings verbatim. Copy inputs and outputs so callers cannot mutate registry state. A failed registration must add neither a host nor a workshop.

Implement a CommonJS module exporting exactly one function, `assembleReaderProfile`.

`assembleReaderProfile(readerId, readers, loans)` builds a detached summary from two collections. A reader is an object with readable fields `{ id, displayName }`; a loan is an object with readable fields `{ readerId, title, returned }`. Fields may be own or inherited. Do not impose closed-field schemas, own-property requirements, prototype restrictions, or plain-object restrictions beyond requiring each record to be a non-null object.

Return:

```js
{
  id: string,
  displayName: string,
  activeTitles: string[]
}
```

Requirements:
- `readerId` must be a string that is non-empty after trimming, or throw `TypeError`. Matching uses the trimmed requested ID.
- `readers` and `loans` must be arrays, or throw `TypeError`.
- Every reader must be a non-null object whose `id` and `displayName` are strings that are non-empty after trimming.
- Every loan must be a non-null object whose `readerId` and `title` are strings with raw length greater than zero and whose `returned` field is a boolean. Whitespace-only loan IDs and titles are valid.
- Validate every element of both arrays, including elements unrelated to the requested reader, before returning either `null` or a profile.
- Compare each trimmed reader ID with the trimmed requested ID. If no reader matches, return `null`; if multiple readers match, use the first one.
- Compare each loan's trimmed `readerId` with the selected reader's trimmed ID. Include matching loans whose `returned` value is `false`.
- Preserve loan order and duplicate titles. Trim every included title; therefore, a valid whitespace-only matching title contributes an empty string.
- Return the selected reader's trimmed `id` and trimmed `displayName`.
- An existing reader with no active loans gets an empty `activeTitles` array.
- Do not mutate either input array or any input object, and do not retain aliases to them in the returned value.

Use no external packages. Export exactly `{ assembleReaderProfile }` using `module.exports`.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.
